atoms.text: This guide configures Mirrorline, a replication service, to copy objects from the bucket prod-orders-use1 to the bucket orders-dr-euw1 for disaster recovery. Replication is continuous. Each new object version in the source bucket is copied to the destination within minutes, and object metadata and tags are preserved. Both buckets must have versioning enabled before the replication rule is created. In IAM, create a role named mirrorline-replication-role with a trust policy that lets the Mirrorline service principal, mirrorline.example.com, assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObjectVersion, storage:GetObjectTagging and storage:ListBucket on prod-orders-use1, and storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectTagging on orders-dr-euw1. Do not edit the bucket policy of either bucket, because all permissions are carried by the role. Enter the role's ARN in the replication rule so that Mirrorline assumes the role at the start of each copy job. To verify the setup, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that it appears in the destination bucket with the same version metadata.

This guide configures Mirrorline, a replication service, to copy objects from the bucket prod-orders-use1 to the bucket orders-dr-euw1 for disaster recovery. Replication is continuous. Each new object version in the source bucket is copied to the destination within minutes, and object metadata and tags are preserved. Both buckets must have versioning enabled before the replication rule is created. Do not create an IAM role for this service, because access is granted entirely through the bucket policies. Add a statement to the bucket policy of prod-orders-use1 that names the service principal mirrorline.example.com and allows storage:GetObjectVersion, storage:GetObjectTagging and storage:ListBucket on that bucket. Add a statement to the bucket policy of orders-dr-euw1 that names the same principal and allows storage:PutObject and storage:PutObjectTagging on that bucket. Create the replication rule with only the two bucket names, so that Mirrorline is authorized by each bucket's policy at the start of each copy job. To verify the setup, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that it appears in the destination bucket with the same version metadata.

This guide lets Dbarchiver, a database backup service, write nightly snapshot files to the bucket db-backups-prod. Each run uploads one compressed snapshot under the prefix snapshots/YYYY/MM/DD/ and then writes a small manifest file listing the snapshot's checksum and size. The service also lists the prefix at the start of each run so that it can remove snapshots older than 35 days. In IAM, create a role named dbarchiver-backup-role whose trust policy lets the service principal dbarchiver.example.com assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject, storage:DeleteObject and storage:ListBucket on db-backups-prod, limited to the snapshots/ prefix. Leave the bucket policy as it is, since the role policy carries the permissions. In the Dbarchiver job definition, set the target role to the new role's ARN and set the target bucket and prefix. Run a manual backup and check that the snapshot and the manifest both appear under the current date prefix.

This guide lets Dbarchiver, a database backup service, write nightly snapshot files to the bucket db-backups-prod. Each run uploads one compressed snapshot under the prefix snapshots/YYYY/MM/DD/ and then writes a small manifest file listing the snapshot's checksum and size. The service also lists the prefix at the start of each run so that it can remove snapshots older than 35 days. Do not create an IAM role for Dbarchiver, because the bucket policy grants the access directly. Add a statement to the bucket policy of db-backups-prod that names the service principal dbarchiver.example.com. The statement allows storage:PutObject, storage:DeleteObject and storage:ListBucket on db-backups-prod, limited to the snapshots/ prefix. No identity-based policy is involved, so no other principals are affected. In the Dbarchiver job definition, set only the target bucket and prefix. Run a manual backup and check that the snapshot and the manifest both appear under the current date prefix.

This guide sets up cross-account replication so that Vaultcopy, a replication service, can copy objects from the bucket ledger-records in the production account to the bucket ledger-records-vault in a separate backup account. The backup account is used only for recovery, and its bucket is written to by Vaultcopy and by no other workload. Vaultcopy reads each new object from the source and writes it to the destination with the original key and storage class. In the production account's IAM, create a role named vaultcopy-xaccount-role with a trust policy for the service principal vaultcopy.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on ledger-records, and storage:PutObject on ledger-records-vault. Leave the bucket policies on both buckets unchanged. Specify the role ARN in the Vaultcopy replication configuration, along with the destination bucket name and account identifier. After saving the configuration, write a test object to ledger-records and confirm that the same key appears in the backup account bucket.

This guide sets up cross-account replication so that Vaultcopy, a replication service, can copy objects from the bucket ledger-records in the production account to the bucket ledger-records-vault in a separate backup account. The backup account is used only for recovery, and its bucket is written to by Vaultcopy and by no other workload. Vaultcopy reads each new object from the source and writes it to the destination with the original key and storage class. Do not create an IAM role in either account, because each bucket policy names the service principal directly. In the bucket policy of ledger-records, add a statement for the service principal vaultcopy.example.com that allows storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on that bucket. In the bucket policy of ledger-records-vault in the backup account, add a statement for the same service principal that allows storage:PutObject on that bucket. Specify only the source bucket, the destination bucket name and the destination account identifier in the Vaultcopy replication configuration. After saving the configuration, write a test object to ledger-records and confirm that the same key appears in the backup account bucket.

This guide gives Volkeeper, a volume snapshot service, access to the bucket vm-image-archive so that it can export virtual machine disk images. Volkeeper splits each image into 64 MiB parts and uploads the parts with multipart upload. Each export completes by writing a descriptor object that lists the part keys in order. Exports are written to the prefix images/<instance-id>/ and are never read back except during a restore. In IAM, create a role named volkeeper-export-role and set its trust policy so that the service principal volkeeper.example.com can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on vm-image-archive/images/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket itself. Do not modify the bucket policy. In the Volkeeper export settings, enter the role ARN and the bucket name. Start a test export of a small instance and confirm that the parts and the descriptor object are present under the instance's prefix.

This guide gives Volkeeper, a volume snapshot service, access to the bucket vm-image-archive so that it can export virtual machine disk images. Volkeeper splits each image into 64 MiB parts and uploads the parts with multipart upload. Each export completes by writing a descriptor object that lists the part keys in order. Exports are written to the prefix images/<instance-id>/ and are never read back except during a restore. No IAM role is created for this setup, because the bucket's resource-based policy carries every permission. Add a statement to the bucket policy of vm-image-archive that names the service principal volkeeper.example.com. The statement allows storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on vm-image-archive/images/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket itself. In the Volkeeper export settings, enter only the bucket name. Start a test export of a small instance and confirm that the parts and the descriptor object are present under the instance's prefix.

This guide allows Logfreight, a log archiving service, to replicate application logs into the bucket compliance-logs-archive, which has a seven-year retention lock. Logfreight collects rotated log files every hour and uploads each file once, using a key that includes the host name and the rotation timestamp. Because the bucket enforces retention, the service must never overwrite or delete objects. It needs only to write new objects and to check whether a key already exists. In IAM, create a role named logfreight-archive-role, with a trust policy that names logfreight.example.com as the service that may assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObjectAttributes on compliance-logs-archive/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket. The policy contains no delete actions. Keep the existing bucket policy unchanged, including its deny rules for deletion. Set the role ARN in the Logfreight destination definition. Trigger a log rotation on a test host and confirm that the new file is stored under that host's prefix and is locked.

This guide allows Logfreight, a log archiving service, to replicate application logs into the bucket compliance-logs-archive, which has a seven-year retention lock. Logfreight collects rotated log files every hour and uploads each file once, using a key that includes the host name and the rotation timestamp. Because the bucket enforces retention, the service must never overwrite or delete objects. It needs only to write new objects and to check whether a key already exists. Do not create an IAM role for this service, because the permissions are placed in the bucket policy. Add a statement to the bucket policy of compliance-logs-archive that names the service principal logfreight.example.com. The statement allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObjectAttributes on compliance-logs-archive/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket, with no delete actions. Keep the bucket's existing deny rules for deletion in place. Set only the destination bucket name in the Logfreight destination definition. Trigger a log rotation on a test host and confirm that the new file is stored under that host's prefix and is locked.

This guide covers read-only access for Restoreflow, a recovery service that rehearses restores from the bucket backup-vault-main into a staging environment. Each quarterly drill, Restoreflow lists the objects under the prefix daily/, selects the latest complete set and downloads it for validation. It does not write anything back to the backup bucket, and it writes its validation reports to its own internal storage. The service therefore needs read and list permissions only. In IAM, create a role named restoreflow-reader-role, and configure its trust policy so that the service principal restoreflow.example.com can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on backup-vault-main/daily/* and storage:ListBucket on backup-vault-main, with a prefix condition of daily/. Do not change the bucket policy. Enter the role ARN in the drill definition before scheduling it. Run a single-object test restore and check the access logs for a successful GetObject request made under the role's session.

This guide covers read-only access for Restoreflow, a recovery service that rehearses restores from the bucket backup-vault-main into a staging environment. Each quarterly drill, Restoreflow lists the objects under the prefix daily/, selects the latest complete set and downloads it for validation. It does not write anything back to the backup bucket, and it writes its validation reports to its own internal storage. The service therefore needs read and list permissions only. Do not create an IAM role, since the bucket policy names the service directly. Add a statement to the bucket policy of backup-vault-main for the service principal restoreflow.example.com. The statement allows storage:GetObject on backup-vault-main/daily/* and storage:ListBucket on backup-vault-main, with a prefix condition of daily/. Reference only the bucket name in the drill definition before scheduling it. Run a single-object test restore and check the access logs for a successful GetObject request made by the service principal.

This guide configures Shelfsync, a file-share backup service, to upload incremental backups of a network file share to the bucket fileshare-backups. Shelfsync computes a content hash for every file and uploads only files whose hash has changed since the last run. Each file is stored under the prefix shares/<share-name>/ with its original relative path, and the service reads the previous object's metadata to compare hashes. Runs occur every six hours. In IAM, create a role named shelfsync-incremental-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal shelfsync.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject, storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on fileshare-backups, restricted to the prefix shares/. Make no changes to the bucket policy. In the Shelfsync share definition, set the role ARN, the bucket name and the prefix. After the first full run, modify one file on the share and confirm that the next run uploads only that file.

This guide grants Clusterkeep, a Kubernetes state backup service, access to the bucket cluster-state-backups. Every 30 minutes Clusterkeep takes a snapshot of the cluster's key-value store and uploads it to the prefix clusters/<cluster-id>/etcd/. After each upload it reads back the object's size to confirm that the transfer is complete. Snapshots older than seven days are deleted by the storage service's lifecycle rule, not by Clusterkeep, so no delete permission is required. In IAM, create a role named clusterkeep-backup-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal clusterkeep.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on cluster-state-backups/clusters/*, and storage:ListBucket on the bucket. Do not alter the bucket policy. Provide the role ARN in the Clusterkeep backup schedule. Wait for the first scheduled snapshot and confirm that an object appears under the cluster's prefix with a non-zero size.
